results.answer: Southwest's 737 MAX 8 fleet of 87 aircraft currently has MCAS v1.7.3 installed on all aircraft, and FAA AD 2024-01-02 requires installation of MCAS v2.0 with a compliance deadline of May 15, 2024; software updates are scheduled February-May 2024 in a phased rollout of roughly 10 aircraft per month. Southwest is compliant with FAA AD 2020-05-11 (all 87 aircraft, pre-service compliance November 2020) and FAA AD 2022-03-07 (all 87 aircraft, completed April 2022). Under 14 CFR Part 39, operators of 737-8 and 737-9 aircraft are legally required to comply with all applicable ADs, and non-compliance results in the aircraft being considered unairworthy. The MCAS v2.0 requirement traces to FAA AD 2024-01-02, issued January 2024. A separate compliance report for aircraft G-ABCD states it is non-compliant with FAA AD 2024-01-02 (deadline not yet reached), with MCAS v1.7.3 installed, a required version of MCAS v2.0 or later, and a scheduled maintenance slot of April 22-23, 2024; that report notes the aircraft remains airworthy under MCAS v1.7.3 until the compliance deadline.
